questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to get fit without spending any money on a gym
Why group exercise at the gym is becoming popular
The history of spin classes and how they began
Why people stop going to the gym after a few weeks
questions.why: Catherine says they're talking about why gym membership and group exercise are becoming more popular.

questions.q: How does Rob prefer to exercise?
options: In a spin class with friends
Playing football in the park
Running alone outdoors
Lifting weights at the gym
questions.why: Rob says he hates group exercise and prefers to go for a run on his own outdoors.

questions.q: Why does Catherine like spin classes?
options: The instructor makes her work harder than alone
They are cheaper than other classes at her gym
She can listen to her favourite music while she cycles
They are very relaxing after a long day at work
questions.why: She says she wouldn't push herself so hard without someone shouting at her.

questions.q: According to Philip Mills, how has our working life changed since the 1960s?
options: We work about 35% fewer hours
More of us work outdoors
Most of us now work from home
We work about 35% more hours
questions.why: He says 'we work about 35% more hours than we used to work in the 60s'.

questions.q: Why does Philip Mills think people go to the gym instead of playing sport together?
options: Society has broken up and lost what brought people together
Gyms are much cheaper than joining a local sports club or team
Parks are too crowded now for team games, especially at weekends
People now prefer to exercise alone, away from friends and family
questions.why: He says society has become fragmented and many things that brought people together no longer exist.

questions.q: Why does Philip Mills say we are 'tribal animals'?
options: To explain why people like competitive sport
To say that people fight too much at the gym
To explain that we still want to feel part of a group
To describe how gyms are organised
questions.why: He says we're pack animals, and the gym helps people commune, meeting our need to belong.

questions.q: What does Philip Mills think group exercise might be like in the future?
options: Classes will be held outdoors
Gyms will close and people will exercise at home
Instructors will become much stricter
People will cycle inside a video game
questions.why: Rob says Mills thinks we'll be cycling inside a video game, visiting other planets and times.

questions.q: What concern does Catherine have about this future idea?
options: It will be too expensive for most ordinary gym members
People will connect with a computer, not each other
It will be less good for our health than outdoor sport
It will be too frightening for children and older people
questions.why: She says people will then be 'communing with a computer', not really with each other.
